steps.title: The question
steps.say: Seasons happen because Earth is tilted. Let's see how.

steps.title: The Sun and its rays
steps.say: The Sun sends light and heat out in straight rays toward Earth.

steps.title: The tilted axis
steps.say: Earth spins on an axis that is tilted about 23.5 degrees.

steps.title: Distance is not the cause
steps.say: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January, so distance is not the reason.

ops.text: Not the distance: Earth is closest to the Sun in January.

steps.title: Northern summer
steps.say: In June the northern half leans toward the Sun, so its rays are more direct and days are longer.

ops.text:
June: north tilts toward the Sun
more direct rays, longer days
= summer

steps.title: Northern winter
steps.say: Six months later the northern half leans away, so the rays are slanted and spread out, making winter.

ops.text:
December: north tilts away
slanted rays, shorter days
= winter

steps.title: Summary
steps.say: Seasons come from the tilt of Earth's axis, not from how far away it is.

ops.text: Tilt causes seasons. Distance barely matters.
